comments.body:
I reviewed the full proof. The overall strategy is correct and most steps are solid:
(A) source M = PX/SL_n is normal (smooth hypersurfaces are properly stable, geometric quotient of a normal variety by a reductive group is normal);
(B) the gradient nabla is a GL_n-equivariant LINEAR injection split by Euler's identity R(p)=(1/d)sum_i x_i p_i, so nabla^# : C[W] -> C[V] is graded-surjective, and by linear reductivity of SL_n the induced map on invariants phi: S=C[W]^G -> R=C[V]^G is graded-surjective;
(C) graded-surjective phi gives a closed immersion iota: Proj R -> Proj S.

GAP FOUND AND FIXED. The original Lemma 'lem:Nopen' claimed N = PZ//G is an OPEN subscheme of Proj S = P(W)//G, i.e. that (PZ)^ss := PZ ∩ P(W)^ss is SATURATED for pi_W. That saturation is not justified and is in general FALSE for an arbitrary invariant open (it would require the unique closed orbit in the semistable closure of each point of (PZ)^ss to lie again in PZ). The subsequent step wrote Pnabla = j^{-1} ∘ (iota|_M), depending on j: N -> Proj S being an open immersion -- unsupported.

FIX (rewritten Section 5): replaced the saturation-dependent argument with one needing only the EXISTENCE of a morphism c: N -> Proj S, never its openness or injectivity:
 - Lemma lem:Ncat: N = (PZ)^ss//G is a categorical quotient, so the SL_n-invariant morphism pi_W|_{(PZ)^ss} factors uniquely through pi_Z, giving c: N -> Proj S with c∘pi_Z = pi_W. (Remark explicitly flags c need not be open.)
 - Lemma lem:Phi-is-iota: nabla induces Phi: Proj R -> Proj S with Phi = Proj(phi) = iota (closed immersion).
 - Prop iso-onto-image, Step 1: c∘Pnabla = iota∘kappa (kappa: M ↪ Proj R the open inclusion), via uniqueness of factorization through the categorical quotient PX -> M.
 - Step 2: iota (closed immersion) and kappa (open immersion) are monomorphisms, so c∘Pnabla = iota∘kappa is a monomorphism; since g∘h mono => h mono, Pnabla is a monomorphism.
 - Step 3: Pnabla is finite (given) hence proper; a PROPER MONOMORPHISM is a CLOSED IMMERSION (EGA IV 18.12.6). Hence Pnabla: M -> Y is an isomorphism and Y ≅ M is normal.

Non-circular: it does not use Zariski's Main Theorem / normality of Y to obtain the isomorphism. Added EGA IV as a reference. Verified symbolically (sympy) that R∘nabla = id and that nabla is GL_n-equivariant. Checked all begin/end environments and \\label/\\ref balance; no dangling references to the removed lemma. (No LaTeX toolchain present to compile.)

Resolving the issue.
